To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the biaxial stress-strain properties of ascending thoracoabdominal aortic aneurisms (TAAAs) are significantly altered from those of healthy ascending aortic tissue.

(1) aortic aneurisms have a biaxial stress-strain behavior that is nonlinear, anisotropic, and heterogeneous; (2) aortic tissue is stiffer and stronger in the circumferential direction than in the axial direction; (3) the circumferential stiffness of aortic aneurism tissue is greater than that of a healthy aortic tissue; (4) aortic aneursims have greater strength in the axial direction than healthy aortic tissue,

(a) aortic aneurisms rupture in a biaxial manner; (b) the biaxial rupture strength is a function of the aneurysm geometry, and is not a function of the material properties of the wall tissue; (c) aneurisms are more likely to rupture in the circumferential direction; and (d) aneurisms that rupture in the longitudinal direction are more likely to do so in the anterior direction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biaxial rupture behavior of ascending aortic aneuryses.
the development of a new approach to the biomechanical analysis of aneurysm rupture, based on the application of a novel biaxial testing device and a new computational model of aneurysmal rupture.
the development of an experimental model to study the biomechanical properties of the aorta.

the biaxial rupture strength of the ascending thoracic aorta is 2-3 times higher than that of the descending aorta, and the rupture strength of the aortic wall increases with age, but decreases with aortic dilatation.
the biaxial rupture behavior of ascending thoracic aneurysms is highly variable and unpredictable.
a biaxial stress-strain curve is the most appropriate way to describe the rupture properties of an ascending thoracic aorta.

we developed a new method to study aortic tissue and found that aortic aneurysl tissue has a unique biaxial rupture behavior.
the biaxial rupture behavior of ascending thoracic aneurysms (AAs) is dependent on the material properties, geometric properties, and the interaction between the material and geometric properties.
aortic wall rupture is a complex process that depends on the interaction of the aortic wall and blood.

the biaxial mechanical properties of ascending thoracics aortic aneuryses (ATA) are significantly different from those of healthy ascending thoracic aortas.
the biaxial rupture strength of aneurysmal ascending thoracic aorta is significantly lower than normal thoracic aorta, but is similar to abdominal aortic aneurism.
aortic aneurisms are more susceptible to failure when the aneurismal wall is subjected to biaxial stress.
